The test image shows a corn leaf with extensive tan/brown necrosis interspersed with remaining green patches, and bleached streaks running lengthwise along the leaf. There are also small white spots visible. This pattern of bleached streaks on a leaf strongly suggests Stewart's Disease or possibly Goss's Wilt.

Let me check one reference image for Stewart's Disease.

The reference for Stewart's Disease shows bleached tan streaks running along the leaf on an otherwise green leaf — matching the early/intermediate stage. The test image shows a more advanced stage: the leaf is mostly necrotic tan/brown with residual green patches and bleached streaks running lengthwise, consistent with the leaf blight phase of Stewart's Disease. The small white dots could be dried bacterial exudate.

The pattern of bleached/tan streaks running the length of the leaf, with progressive blight and some green tissue remaining, aligns well with Stewart's Disease description: "Bleached leaf streaks running the length of the leaf in early phase, progressing to leaf blight after tasseling."
